rs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, May 13, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I have to refer to your letter of the 3rd ultimo with, regard to the payment by this Department of an
amount of $1,500 to Messrs. Guite & Co., general merchants of Maria, Quebec, for relief supplied to Indians of that
reserve between 1918 and 1921. This, firm submitted their accounts to the Department from time to time. In view of
the fact that the Indian Agent had not reported on the. matter it was considered necessary to have. a careful
investigation. Accordingly Mr. Chéné was sent to Maria for that purpose, being specialty qualified therefor as a
bilinguist. He found that the supplies in question were issued to the Indians, for the most part, under emergency
conditions during the successive epidemic of influenza. I am not aware of any legal status. that Messrs. Guite would
have as against the Department with respect to these accounts. It is clear, however, that it was absolutely necessary that
the supplies, should be issued in order to alleviate distress, and to save the lives of the Indians who were sick and
destitute. The Department, therefore, could not view the matter in its strictly legal aspect, being concerned rather with
the urgency of the conditions. In checking over the accounts Mr. Chéné passed only those items which seemed
absolutely necessary. These the Department feels, morally bound to recognize. It was with this proper discrimination
that the amount of $1,500 was arrived at. The records of the



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 589-592) ===
<!-- page 589 -->
Department show that the accounts have not been paid previously and that there has been no duplication of payment.

I trust that this explanation of the matter will satisfy your requirements.


Yours truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Indian Trust Fund: Payment for Medical Attendance during absence of Regular Medical Officer


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 19, 1924.

SIR, - Indian Trust Fund cheque No. 3466, is for the payment of $20 to Dr. J. Rogers of Forest, Ont., for medical
services rendered an Indian woman during the absence of Dr. McDonald, the regular medical officer, who was
attending a medical convention at Toronto.

As Dr. McDonald is in receipt of an annual salary as Indian physician, should not he have made arrangements for his
Indian patients being attended to during his absence without additional cost to the Indians or to your Department.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, June 24, 1924.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 19th instant, pointing out that Dr. McDonald, under salary
as medical attendant to the Indians of Kettle & Stony Point Band, should bear the cost of medical attendance which
was necessary during his absence at a medical convention. In reply I would say that Dr. McDonald, as, Medical Health
Officer of the district attended the convention of that body with the knowledge of the Indian Agent, and an emergent
case developed on the reserve so that Dr. Rogers had to be called in to save life.

It is not the practice of this Department to allow holidays to part time officers, but it is considered that Dr. McDonald
in leaving his Indian patients for a few days, to attend a medical convention should not be asked to pay for necessary
attendance during his absence, as he would be in a better position to render efficient service from meeting with the
members of his profession.

Had Dr. McDonald gone on a pleasure jaunt his absence would be regarded differently, but under the circumstances, I
consider the Department was quite justified in paying for the emergency case and not making the same a charge
against Dr. McDonald's salary.

Dr. McDonald's salary is only $33.33 a month and to charge against this $20 for one case during his short absence
would not be considered just or reasonable. The Department has found Dr. McDonald's services to the Indians under
his care very satisfactory.

<!-- page 590 -->
Your obedient servant,
J.D. MCLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Sec'y.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Indian Trust Fund, Assiniboine Reserve: Repayment of Balance of loan from Home Bank


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, August 7, 1924.

SIR, - Indian Trust Fund Cheque No. 685, issued on April 20, 1923, is for the payment of $511 to the Home Bank of
Canada, Sintaluta branch, for "Balance of loan from bank with interests for purpose of paying for twine and threshing
expenses, Assiniboine farmers, August 18 and September 17, 1920."

While this is all the information I have with regard to this loan, I infer that in 1920 a loan was affected from the Home
Bank for the,purpose of aiding the Indians in their farming operations, that the money so obtained was placed by the
agent in a special or trust account and paid out there from without any report of such expenditure being made to this
office, and that repayments were made to the bank from time to time from moneys collected from the Indians.

If the above inference is a correct one I should like to have a full statement of all the transactions connected with the
loan in question; if it is not a correct inference kindly advise me of the actual facts of the case.

Kindly let me know under what authority this loan was effected, and if the present was an isolated case or if it is a
general practice for the agents to obtain loans from the banks to enable the Indians to carry on farming or other
operations.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, August 15, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 7th instant, I beg to say that in August and September, 1920, Air. Indian
Agent Wilson, of Sintaluta, obtained loans aggregating $800.00 from the Home Bank in order that he might obtain
twine and pay threshing accounts, etc., on behalf of Indians of the Assiniboine Reserve. He acted in the matter without
the Department's knowledge, but he accounted for the transactions in his Agency cash book, as will be seen from the
attached statement taken from his returns, which statement is supported by receipts herewith transmitted.

When the matter came to the Department's attention, payments totalling $406.46 bad been made by the Agent to the
Bank in refund of loans.

As it was doubtful when the Indians would be able to repay the balance of the money due, the Department informed
Mr. Commissioner Graham, who had been written to in the matter, that the balance of loan should be retired without
delay, and, consequently, a voucher No. 7275, for $511.00 was presented by Mr. Wilson and was, paid by cheque
No. 685 which was drawn against account No. 145.

When issuing instructions for the issue of the cheque, the Department requested Mr. Graham to notify all the Indian
Agents in the Western Provinces that they must not negotiate loans through the Banks or in any other way in future. It
was further stated that if funds are required to finance a project the whole matter should be laid before the Department
with a definite recommendation. Mr. Graham acted upon these instructions.

So far as the Department is aware, loans from Banks have not been obtained by other Indian Agents.


Yours truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

<!-- page 592 -->
The Auditor General.
